question.text: An investor sells Sovereign Gold Bonds after 20 months at a profit, in a transfer (not redemption). How will the capital gains be classified and taxed?

answer.text: STCG taxed at the investor's income tax slab rate, since holding period is 24 months or less
LTCG taxed at 12.5% without indexation, since holding period exceeds 12 months
Fully exempt from capital gains tax as it is a government security
STCG taxed at a flat rate of 15%

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that on transfer of SGBs, gains are LTCG if the bonds are held for more than 12 months and STCG only if held within 12 months, and the same taxability applies to off-market transactions. A 20-month holding therefore qualifies as LTCG, taxable at 12.5% without indexation. The Trap: Slab-rate STCG only applies inside the 12-month window; a blanket exemption applies only to redemption with RBI (not transfers); and the 15% flat rate is a listed-equity STCG rate, not the SGB transfer rate. Note: Based on NISM Series X-B workbook pp.266-267, which set out the SGB transfer holding-period rule and tax rate.
